lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Caring for Home and Shared Spaces
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: ten-minute reset

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice ten-minute reset. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult first walks the learner through a ten-minute reset of one shared space, narrating each of four steps out loud: clear the surfaces, sort items into keep-here or belongs-elsewhere, return the belongs-elsewhere items to their homes, and wipe down the cleared surface.
safetyNotes: Use respectful, non-shaming language about the starting condition of either space.

simulationAlternative.description: If no second shared space is available to reset independently, the learner instead resets the same first space a second time on a different day, timing themselves and comparing their independent time against the adult-modeled time.

materials: learner-local: basket or bag for sorting

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: What is one thing about the four-step order (clear, sort, return, wipe) that made the reset go faster than just cleaning without a set order?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Following the four-step order: Completes all four steps in the modeled order. | Timing and pacing awareness: Accurately names which step took longest. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner time a reset in a third, messier shared space and write down one change they'd make to the four-step order for a space that messy.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice ten-minute reset. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: timer or clock
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: basket or bag for sorting
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: ten-minute reset worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult first walks the learner through a ten-minute reset of one shared space, narrating each of four steps out loud: clear the surfaces, sort items into keep-here or belongs-elsewhere, return the belongs-elsewhere items to their homes, and wipe down the cleared surface.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact ten-minute reset decision or action.
Model move 2: Before the model, predict which of the four reset steps you think will take the most time in this space and why.
Model move 3: Watch and help with the adult's ten-minute reset of the first space, naming which of the four steps is happening as you go.
Model check: Following the four-step order: Completes all four steps in the modeled order. | Timing and pacing awareness: Accurately names which step took longest.

resources.title: ten-minute reset action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for ten-minute reset.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: ten-minute reset coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult first walks the learner through a ten-minute reset of one shared space, narrating each of four steps out loud: clear the surfaces, sort items into keep-here or belongs-elsewhere, return the belongs-elsewhere items to their homes, and wipe down the cleared surface.
Coach direction: Before the model, predict which of the four reset steps you think will take the most time in this space and why.
Learner prompt: Name the step you predict will take longest and give one reason.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: ten-minute reset complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Watch and help with the adult's ten-minute reset of the first space, naming which of the four steps is happening as you go.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I could name the current step (clear, sort, return, or wipe) at least three separate times.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I helped with at least one full step alongside the adult.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I noticed one item that didn't have an obvious 'home' to return to.

Equal-access rule: If no second shared space is available to reset independently, the learner instead resets the same first space a second time on a different day, timing themselves and comparing their independent time against the adult-modeled time.

resources.title: ten-minute reset minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is one thing about the four-step order (clear, sort, return, wipe) that made the reset go faster than just cleaning without a set order?
Success checks: Following the four-step order: Completes all four steps in the modeled order. | Timing and pacing awareness: Accurately names which step took longest.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: ten-minute reset supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional ten-minute reset condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Following the four-step order: Completes all four steps in the modeled order. | Timing and pacing awareness: Accurately names which step took longest..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: A trusted adult first walks the learner through a ten-minute reset of one shared space, narrating each of four steps out loud: clear the surfaces, sort items into keep-here or belongs-elsewhere, return the belongs-elsewhere items to their homes, and wipe down the cleared surface.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Name the step you predict will take longest and give one reason.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Following the four-step order: Completes all four steps in the modeled order.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

realRoute.title: ten-minute reset — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Watch and help with the adult's ten-minute reset of the first space, naming which of the four steps is happening as you go.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: ten-minute reset — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If no second shared space is available to reset independently, the learner instead resets the same first space a second time on a different day, timing themselves and comparing their independent time against the adult-modeled time.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: What is one thing about the four-step order (clear, sort, return, wipe) that made the reset go faster than just cleaning without a set order?
observableCriteria: Following the four-step order: Completes all four steps in the modeled order.
Timing and pacing awareness: Accurately names which step took longest.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Following the four-step order: Completes all four steps in the modeled order. | Timing and pacing awareness: Accurately names which step took longest.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
